name: MD-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+30 partisan lean makes it one of the most Democratic House seats
Raskin holds an overwhelming financial edge: about $8.1 million on hand versus roughly $3,200 for Riley
High-profile incumbent seeking re-election with no competitive general-election history
Prediction markets price Democratic odds near 97% with no contrary signals
model.rationale: The district's D+30 lean, Raskin's massive fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 97% Democratic all point the same direction, and no polls or ratings suggest competition. The Green Party candidate may draw a few points but cannot alter the outcome.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary external shock to the incumbent, such as a major scandal or health event, would put this seat in any doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 8th District is one of the most Democratic House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+30. Jamie Raskin, a high-profile incumbent first elected in 2016, has won re-election by wide margins and is seeking another term. Republican Cheryl Riley has run a minimal campaign, reporting about $22,000 raised and $3,200 on hand, while Raskin holds more than $8 million in cash. A Green Party candidate is also on the ballot but shows no measurable support.

Prediction markets put Democratic odds near 97%, and no expert ratings flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on the district's fundamentals, which point to a margin of roughly 30 points. The seat is rated Safe D, and the main question is the size of the victory rather than the winner.
